01.actor: the daughter-in-law of the house of bar Elyashiv
01.event: she sues the orphans for her ketubah and goes to court in house clothes
01.turn: the orphans object that it shames them, so she dresses in all her clothes
01.outcome: before Ravina, who rules that a widow's clothes on her are appraised against her ketubah
01.summary: A widow claimed her ketubah from her husband's orphans and was bringing them to court. They said it shamed them that she go dressed as she was, so she put on all her clothes. When they came before Ravina, he ruled that the clothes she wore are appraised, so her compliance cost her.
01.reason: There is an incident with several actions (claim, objection, dressing, appearing in court) and a ruling that turns the orphans' request against her; more than coming before a rabbi.

02.event: a woman comes before Rava saying her husband died in a famine
02.turn: under cross-examination she reveals she did not see him die
02.outcome: Rava reverses his ruling that famine is not like war
02.summary: Rava held that famine differs from war for a wife's testimony. A woman came and said her husband died in a famine; Rava probed her and she answered that he could not have survived. From this Rava changed his mind and ruled famine is like war.
02.missing: any action beyond the woman's coming and the exchange of words
02.reason: One real event (the woman coming to testify) and then mainly dialogue, though it produces a change in Rava's ruling; sits between borderline and not, so borderline.

03.missing: an event: the passage is a halakhic dilemma, a search of sources, and a ruling sent out
03.reason: A question, a search of the baraitot, a rejection and a sent ruling are ordinary scholarly process and speech, with no narrated event or conflict.

04.outcome: he says business is better than farming; nothing follows
04.summary: Rav walked among the sheaves, saw them waving, and told them that business was better than they were.
04.missing: any consequence or change; the act only frames a dictum
04.reason: A single act framing a saying, with nothing following; a bare report leading nowhere.

05.missing: a one-time event; this is a household practice and a ruling
05.reason: A habitual use of a beam that R. Pedat did not object to, cited as his ruling; a custom that leads nowhere.

06.event: a yevama comes to perform halitza before R. Tarfon
06.turn: he instructs the students to respond aloud
06.summary: R. Yehuda recalled sitting before R. Tarfon when a yevama came to perform halitza, and R. Tarfon told them all to respond 'He who had his shoe removed.'
06.missing: any action or change beyond the arrival and the instruction
06.reason: One event (the yevama arriving) followed by an instruction, cited as a legal source; under R-C0's limit this is not a story.

07.event: R. Eliezer missed the study hall and met R. Asi
07.turn: he asks what was said and gets R. Yohanan's ruling
07.outcome: he raises an inference; discussion follows
07.summary: R. Eliezer had not gone to the study hall, met R. Asi and asked what was taught; R. Asi reported R. Yohanan's ruling and R. Eliezer drew an inference.
07.missing: an event beyond the setting; it is a question and answer
07.reason: A setting plus a question and answer is not a story (Shabbat 147a line).

08.event: he is afflicted by suskhinta from Rav Huna's long lectures
08.turn: they hang him from the study hall's cedar and green matter comes out
08.outcome: he alone of sixty elders escapes impotence
08.summary: Several sages became impotent from holding themselves during Rav Huna's discourses. Rav Aha bar Yaakov contracted the disease, was suspended from the cedar post of the study hall, and a green substance came out of him. He said that of sixty elders he alone was spared.
08.reason: An affliction, a treatment, and a cure with a stated outcome: two or more events with causality and change.

09.event: Rav Safra challenges the joint Shabbat limit of Akistefon and Ardeshir
09.turn: Rava goes out and shows him the submerged wall foundations
09.summary: Rav Safra asked Rava how the two cities could share a Shabbat limit with the Tigris between them. Rava went out and showed him wall foundations submerged in the river, linking the cities.
09.missing: change beyond resolving a legal question
09.reason: Mainly a question and answer, but with one real event (going out and showing the wall); between borderline and not, so borderline.

10.missing: a one-time event; only practices of biblical women and the Sages' non-protest
10.reason: A report of habitual practices (Michal's tefillin, Jonah's wife's pilgrimage) cited as evidence, with no event following; also about biblical figures.

11.actor: Rabbi and R. Yishmael; R. Yohanan
11.event: a case of a deserted wife came before each
11.turn: they ruled oppositely on sustenance; R. Yohanan wondered
11.outcome: Rav Shemen reports Shmuel's interpretation; R. Yohanan is astonished
11.summary: A case came before Rabbi and before R. Yishmael, who ruled differently on a wife's sustenance. R. Yohanan questioned one ruling and Rav Shemen bar Abba cited Shmuel's explanation, which astonished R. Yohanan.
11.missing: any event in the cases beyond coming before a rabbi and the ruling
11.reason: Cases brought before rabbis and ruled on, then scholarly discussion; coming before a rabbi is the only event.

12.actor: Rav Anan bar Tahalifa; Rav Ashi
12.event: standing before his master when a craved dish was brought
12.outcome: he would have been endangered otherwise
12.summary: Rav Anan bar Tahalifa recalled standing before Mar Shmuel when mushrooms were brought; had Shmuel not given him some he would have been endangered. Rav Ashi tells the same of Rav Kahana and turnip slices.
12.missing: real change; the danger is counterfactual
12.reason: Two events (dish brought, given) but little change, cited as evidence for a rule; weak causality, so borderline rather than not.

13.actor: Rabbi on his deathbed; the people of Bireta DeSatya
13.event: a ditch overflows with fish and they trap them on Shabbat
13.turn: R. Ahai b. R. Yoshiya excommunicates them
13.summary: As Rabbi lay dying he spoke of places in Babylonia. Of Bireta DeSatya he said they had turned from God that day: a fish ditch overflowed, they caught the fish on Shabbat, R. Ahai excommunicated them, and they apostatized.
13.reason: The deathbed speech contains a narrated sequence of actions with causality and a change (excommunication leading to apostasy).

14.event: they carried a woman out on a bier
14.summary: Cited as proof that seclusion with ten immoral men is not safe: there was an incident where ten men carried out a woman on a bier.
14.missing: what happened and why; the incident is only alluded to and filled in by the translation
14.reason: An incident alluded to as evidence, reconstructable only with commentary; R-C6 makes it borderline.

15.event: he declares the state of Babylonian places, including the Shabbat fishing and apostasy at Bireta DeSatya
15.turn: he announces Adda bar Ahava's circumcision and Rav Yehuda's birth that day
15.outcome: the Gemara comments that a righteous man is born as another dies
15.summary: Dying, Rabbi spoke of Babylonian places; at Bireta DeSatya the people fished on Shabbat, were excommunicated by R. Ahai and apostatized. He added that Adda bar Ahava was being circumcised that day and Rav Yehuda was born. The Gemara then generalizes about the succession of the righteous.
15.reason: The deathbed scene contains a full embedded incident with change; segment 4 is the Gemara's commentary and not part of the story.

16.actor: a certain man; Rav Aha bar Huna; Rav Yosef
16.event: a man betrothed a woman with a myrtle branch in the marketplace
16.turn: the case is sent to Rav Yosef
16.outcome: Rav Yosef orders him flogged and requires a get
16.summary: A man betrothed a woman in the marketplace with a myrtle branch. Rav Aha bar Huna sent the case to Rav Yosef, who replied to flog him and require a bill of divorce.
16.missing: whether the flogging or divorce happened; any change narrated
16.reason: One event followed by a sent ruling; the order only implies the outcome, which R-C0 says does not count.

17.event: Rav Yosef says he never heard a ruling
17.turn: Abaye reminds him he taught it himself
17.summary: Rav Yosef said he had not heard a ruling, and Abaye told him he himself had taught it, citing the context.
17.missing: an event; the illness and forgetting come only from the translator's gloss
17.reason: A dialogue of ordinary scholarly correction with no event narrated in the text itself.

18.event: a feather lands on Ameimar's head while judging; spittle lies before Mar Ukva
18.turn: a man removes the feather / covers the spittle, then says he has a case
18.outcome: each judge disqualifies himself from that man's case
18.summary: While Ameimar sat judging, a feather landed on his head and a man removed it; asked his business, he said he had a case, and Ameimar recused himself. Likewise a man covered spittle before Mar Ukva, revealed he had a case, and Mar Ukva recused himself.
18.reason: Each episode has an action, a reveal, and a consequence (recusal) caused by the action: two actions and change.

19.event: Ulla, who used to go up to the Land, dies outside it
19.turn: R. Elazar laments; told the coffin is coming, he answers it is not the same
19.outcome: Ulla's death abroad stands as a loss
19.summary: Ulla regularly went up to Eretz Yisrael but died abroad. When told, R. Elazar applied to him 'you shall die in an unclean land'; told that his coffin was being brought, he said burial after death is not like being received by the Land alive.
19.reason: A death, the report, a lament, and the bringing of the coffin: events with a response and change, not a bare report.

20.actor: a woman litigant; Rav Beivai bar Abaye; Rav Pappi
20.event: a woman obligated to swear in Rav Beivai's court
20.turn: the opponent asks for a public oath; she demands a document first; Rav Beivai agrees
20.outcome: Rav Pappi mocks Rav Beivai's ruling
20.summary: A woman owed an oath in Rav Beivai bar Abaye's court; her opponent wanted her to swear in town hoping she would admit, and she demanded a document of rights in advance. Rav Beivai told them to write it, and Rav Pappi derided him for it.
20.missing: any action beyond the court exchange
20.reason: After the woman comes to court it is all dialogue, with some conflict in Rav Pappi's rebuke; mainly speech with one event, so borderline.
